p.src: After Baoyu had seen Jia Zheng and returned to his room, his head felt still dizzier and more oppressed. Too listless to move, he did not even eat, but sank into a heavy sleep. Doctors were again summoned to examine and treat him, but their medicines had no effect, until at last he could no longer even recognize those around him. When everyone helped him sit up, however, he still looked like a healthy man. Several days passed in this turmoil. Then came the appointed day for the newlyweds’ ninth-day visit. If they did not go, Aunt Xue would lose face; yet if they did, Baoyu was in such a state. Grandmother Jia knew perfectly well that his illness had arisen because of Daiyu. She wanted to tell him the truth, but feared that the shock might provoke a dangerous turn. As Baochai was a new bride, it was difficult for her to offer him comfort; it would be best if her mother could come over. But if they omitted the ninth-day visit, Aunt Xue would take offense. So Grandmother Jia consulted Lady Wang and Xifeng, saying, “It seems to me that Baoyu’s wits have simply deserted him. There should be no harm in moving him. Have two small sedan chairs brought, and let the servants support them as they cross through the garden. That will fulfill the auspicious observance of the ninth-day visit. Afterwards we can ask Aunt Xue to come and comfort Baochai, while all of us devote ourselves to treating Baoyu. Would that not satisfy both needs?” Lady Wang agreed, and preparations were made at once. Fortunately, Baochai was a new bride and Baoyu was delirious and witless, so the others were able to maneuver them through the ceremony as they pleased. Baochai too knew the truth. In her heart she blamed her mother for having handled the matter so foolishly, but now that things had come to this, she refused to say more. Aunt Xue alone, seeing Baoyu in this condition, bitterly regretted what had been done; but she could only bring the occasion to a hasty close.

p.src: After returning home, Baoyu’s condition grew still more serious, and by the next day he could not even sit up. He worsened from day to day, until he could no longer take even broth or water. Aunt Xue and the others were thrown into a panic. They summoned renowned physicians from everywhere, but none could identify the source of the illness. There was, however, an impoverished physician named Bi, styled Zhi’an, who lived in a dilapidated temple outside the city. He diagnosed the cause as violent alternations of grief and joy, an imbalance of cold and heat, irregular meals, and pent-up sorrow and resentment obstructing the vital energy: an illness arising from both internal injury and external influence. He calculated the proper prescription and administered it that evening. Sure enough, after the second watch Baoyu regained some awareness and asked for water. Only then did Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others feel relieved. They asked Aunt Xue to bring Baochai and rest for the time being in Grandmother Jia’s quarters.

p.src: Baoyu remained lucid for a short while and felt that he might not survive. When everyone had left and only Xiren remained in the room, he called her to his side, took her hand, and wept: “Tell me, how did Cousin Bao come here? I remember Father marrying me to Cousin Lin. How was it that Cousin Bao drove her away? Why has she taken possession of this place? I want to speak of it, but I am afraid of offending her. How terribly did you hear Cousin Lin weeping?” Xiren dared not tell him the truth and could only say, “Miss Lin is ill.” “I shall go and see her,” said Baoyu. With that, he tried to rise. But after taking no food for so many days, how could his body move? He began to cry: “I am going to die! There is something in my heart that I must tell you. I beg you to report it to the Old Lady: Cousin Lin is going to die in any case, and now there is no assurance that I shall live either. With two sick people in two separate places both about to die, it will be all the harder to make arrangements after we are gone. It would be better to clear out an empty room and have Cousin Lin and me carried there at once. While we live, we can be treated and cared for together; when we die, our bodies can be laid out together. If you do as I ask, you will not have failed the affection we have shared all these years.” At these words, Xiren wept until sobs choked her throat and she could scarcely breathe. Just then Baochai came in with Ying’er and heard him. She said, “Instead of resting and nursing your illness, why must you say such ill-omened things? The Old Lady has only just been somewhat comforted, and now you are causing fresh trouble. All her life the Old Lady has cherished you above everyone else, and now she is over eighty. She does not covet an honorary title through you, but if one day you make a man of yourself, then she will have the joy of seeing it, if only for a day, and all her loving care will not have been in vain. As for your mother, there is even less need to speak of it. She has spent the devotion and strength of a lifetime raising you, her one son. If you were to die before your time, what would become of her? Though my fate may be unfortunate, it has surely not come to this. Judging from these three considerations, even if you wished to die, Heaven itself would not allow it. Therefore, you simply must not die. Just rest quietly. After four or five days of nursing, the harmful wind will disperse and your harmonious vital energy will be fully restored; then all these strange ailments will naturally vanish.” Baoyu found himself quite unable to answer her. After a long while he gave a foolish little laugh and said, “You have not spoken to me for ever so long. Whom are you addressing with all these grand principles now?” Hearing this, Baochai continued, “Then I shall tell you the truth. During those two days when you were unconscious, Cousin Lin passed away.” Baoyu suddenly sat upright and cried out in astonishment, “Is she truly dead?” “She is truly dead,” Baochai replied. How could I utter such words merely to curse a living person with death?

p.src: Suddenly everything before his eyes went pitch-black, and he could no longer tell which way to go. As he stood there dazed, he seemed to see someone approaching and asked bewilderedly, “May I ask what place this is?” The man replied, “This is the road to the springs of the underworld. Your allotted years are not yet ended. Why have you come here?” Baoyu said, “I have just heard that an old friend has died, so I came here seeking her and lost my way without realizing it.” The man asked, “Who is this old friend?” Baoyu replied, “Lin Daiyu of Gusu.” The man sneered. “Lin Daiyu was unlike ordinary mortals in life and unlike ordinary ghosts in death. She has neither soul nor spirit—where could you hope to find her? The souls and spirits of ordinary people gather to form the body and disperse into vital breath: gathered in life, they scatter at death. Even an ordinary person cannot be found after death, much less Lin Daiyu. Go back at once.” Baoyu listened and stood dumbfounded for a long while before asking, “If, as you say, the dead disperse, how can this underworld exist?” The man sneered. “The underworld exists when one says it does and does not when one says it does not. Because worldly people are mired in notions of life and death, such tales were devised to admonish them. Thus it is said that Heaven is deeply angered by fools who refuse to remain content with their proper lot, who take their own lives before their allotted span and fortune are exhausted, or who, addicted to lust, violence, and cruelty, destroy themselves without cause. This hell was specially established to imprison their souls and spirits and make them endure boundless suffering in atonement for the sins of their lives. By seeking Daiyu, you are casting yourself into it without cause. Besides, Daiyu has already returned to the Land of Illusion in the Great Void. If you truly wish to seek her, devote yourself to spiritual cultivation, and in time you will naturally meet again. But if you will not live peacefully, you will be imprisoned in the underworld for the crime of cutting short your own life; then, apart from your parents, you will never be able to see Daiyu, however much you may wish it.” When he had finished speaking, the man took a stone from his sleeve and hurled it at Baoyu’s chest. Frightened by these words and by the stone striking him over the heart, Baoyu wanted to return home at once, but to his dismay he had lost the way. While he was hesitating, he suddenly heard someone calling him from nearby. He turned and saw none other than Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, Baochai, Xiren, and the others gathered around him, weeping and calling his name. He himself was still lying on his bed. On the table a red lamp glowed, and beyond the window shone the bright moon: he was still amid brocade splendor in the bustling world of the living. When he collected himself and reflected, he realized it had all been a great dream. He was drenched in cold sweat, yet felt clear and refreshed within. Thinking it over carefully, he saw that there was truly nothing he could do and merely heaved several long sighs. Baochai had long known that Daiyu was dead. Grandmother Jia and the others had forbidden anyone to tell Baoyu, fearing that the news would worsen his illness beyond cure. Baochai herself, however, understood perfectly that his illness had arisen chiefly from Daiyu and only secondarily from the loss of the jade. She had therefore seized the opportunity to tell him plainly, hoping that one decisive agony would end his uncertainty, reunite his scattered faculties, and perhaps make a cure possible. Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others did not understand Baochai’s purpose and severely reproached her for acting so rashly. Only when they later saw Baoyu regain consciousness did they finally feel relieved.

p.src: At first Xiren deeply resented Baochai for having told him, though she could not very well say so aloud. Even Yinger privately told Baochai, “Miss, you were far too hasty.” Baochai replied, “What do you know? Whatever happens, I am here to bear it.” Baochai paid no heed to anyone’s criticism. She merely observed Baoyu’s sickness of the heart and quietly applied the needed remedy. As the days passed, Baoyu gradually felt his mind grow steadier, though whenever Daiyu came to mind he still became confused. Moreover, Xiren often gently reasoned with him: “The Master chose Miss Bao because she is kind and generous, while he disliked Miss Lin’s peculiar temperament and had always feared she would die young. The Old Lady was afraid that, not knowing what was best for you, you would become agitated during your illness, so she had Xueyan come and deceive you.” Even so, Baoyu could not help shedding bitter tears. He wanted to seek death, but then remembered the words spoken in his dream. He also feared angering the Old Lady and Lady Wang, and so could not cast everything aside. Then he reflected that Daiyu was dead and Baochai was a woman of the very highest worth. At last he accepted that his marriage ordained by gold and jade had been fated, and his heart found considerable relief. Seeing that no serious harm was likely, Baochai felt reassured as well. After duly performing all the family courtesies before Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others, she began devising ways to ease Baoyu’s sorrow. Though Baoyu was still unable to sit up often, he frequently saw Baochai seated by his bedside, and his inborn old weakness could not help but stir within him. Baochai always counseled him with proper words, comforting him by saying, “Recovering your health is what matters. Now that you and I are husband and wife, why need we hurry?” Though Baoyu remained unhappy at heart, Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, Aunt Xue, and the others took turns keeping him company by day; at night Baochai retired alone, while Grandmother Jia assigned attendants to care for him. He therefore had no choice but to set his mind at rest and quietly recuperate. And seeing Baochai’s gentle ways, he gradually transferred a little of the love he had borne Daiyu to her—but that belongs later in the story.

p.src: Now, on the day Baoyu married, Daiyu had already fallen unconscious during the daytime, yet the faintest thread of breath still lingered in her chest and on her lips, while Li Wan and Zijuan wept themselves nearly to death. By evening Daiyu revived once more and opened her eyes slightly, seeming to want water or broth. By then Xueyan had gone, leaving only Zijuan and Li Wan at her side. Zijuan brought a bowl of pear juice mixed with longan broth and fed her two or three spoonfuls with a small silver spoon. Daiyu rested quietly for a while with her eyes closed, feeling as though her mind hovered between clarity and darkness. Seeing Daiyu rally a little, Li Wan knew perfectly well that this was the last flicker of the lamp before it went out. Yet she judged that Daiyu could hold on for another half-day, so she returned to Paddy-Sweet Cottage to attend to some matters.

p.src: Daiyu opened her eyes and looked about. Seeing only Zijuan, her nurse, and several young maids there, she seized Zijuan's hand and said with an effort, “I am of no use anymore. You have waited on me for several years, and I had always hoped that the two of us would remain together forever. I never thought that I…” As she spoke, she panted for a while longer, then closed her eyes to rest. Zijuan saw that Daiyu gripped her hand and would not release it, so she dared not move. Daiyu seemed somewhat better than she had that morning, and Zijuan had supposed she might yet recover; but these words chilled her hopes by half once more. After a long while, Daiyu said again, “Dear sister, I have no family here. My body is still pure. Whatever happens, see that they send me home.” Having said this, she closed her eyes again and spoke no more. Yet her hand gradually tightened, and her breathing came in a continuous gasp: each exhalation was heavy, each inhalation faint, and her distress had already become acute.

p.src: Zijuan grew alarmed and hurriedly sent someone to fetch Li Wan. Just then, by good fortune, Tanchun arrived. As soon as Zijuan saw her, she whispered urgently, “Third Young Mistress, please look at Miss Lin.” As she spoke, her tears fell like rain. Tanchun came over and felt Daiyu's hand. It was already cold, and even her gaze had become unfocused. While Tanchun and Zijuan wept and called for water to wash Daiyu, Li Wan hurried in. The three had only just met and had no time to speak. They had scarcely begun washing her when Daiyu suddenly cried out in a piercing voice, “Baoyu! Baoyu! How you…” At the word “how,” cold sweat broke over her whole body, and she fell silent. Zijuan and the others hastily supported her. The sweat poured out ever more heavily, and her body gradually grew cold. Tanchun and Li Wan had the maids hurriedly arrange her hair and dress her. Then Daiyu's eyes rolled upward—and alas! One wisp of her fragrant soul scattered upon the wind; at the third watch, her grief drifted far into dreams.

p.src: The moment when Daiyu breathed her last was precisely the hour when Baoyu was marrying Baochai. Zijuan and the others all burst into loud weeping. Li Wan and Tanchun thought how lovable she had always been, and how much more pitiable she was today, and they too wept bitterly from the heart. As the Xiaoxiang Lodge stood far from the bridal chamber, no one over there heard them. After everyone had wept for some time, they heard a strain of music far in the distance; but when they strained their ears to listen, it was gone. Tanchun and Li Wan went out into the courtyard to listen again, but there was only the wind stirring the tips of the bamboo and the moon's shadow shifting across the wall—a scene of utter desolation and chill. Presently they summoned Lin Zhixiao's wife. After Daiyu's body had been properly laid out, someone was assigned to keep watch, and they resolved to report the matter to Xifeng the following morning.

p.src: Xifeng saw that Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others were in turmoil, that Jia Zheng was about to depart, and that Baoyu had grown still more delirious. At this moment of extraordinary anxiety, she feared that if Daiyu's death were reported as well, the combined grief might make Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang fall ill. She therefore had no choice but to go to the Garden herself. When she reached the Xiaoxiang Lodge, she too could not help weeping for a while. When she saw Li Wan and Tanchun and learned that everything had been arranged, she said, “Very good. But why did neither of you say anything just now and leave me so anxious?” Tanchun replied, “We were seeing Father off just then. How could we have spoken?” Xifeng said, “At least you two have shown her some compassion. As things stand, I must go back over there and attend to that ill-fated one. But this matter is terribly awkward. It cannot go unreported today, yet if I do report it, I fear the Old Lady will not be able to bear the shock.” Li Wan said, “Go and act according to circumstances. Report it only when the moment is right.” Xifeng nodded and hurried away.

p.src: When Xifeng returned to Baoyu's rooms, she heard the physician say there was no cause for alarm, and Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang felt somewhat relieved. Keeping the news from Baoyu, Xifeng then slowly explained what had happened to Daiyu. Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang were both badly startled by the news. Tears streaming down her face, Grandmother Jia said, “It was I who ruined her. But that girl was far too foolish!” As she spoke, she made to go into the Garden and weep over Daiyu, but she was also worried about Baoyu and could not attend to both at once. Suppressing their own grief, Lady Wang and the others joined in urging Grandmother Jia not to go. “Your health is what matters most, Old Lady.” Helpless, Grandmother Jia could only tell Lady Wang to go in her place. She added, “Tell her departed spirit for me: ‘It is not because I am heartless that I have not come to see you off, but because even among kin, some are nearer than others. You are my daughter's child and very dear to me; yet compared with Baoyu, Baoyu is a little nearer still. If anything should happen to Baoyu, how could I face his father?’” With that, she began to weep again. Lady Wang consoled her, saying, “Miss Lin was the one you cherished most, Old Lady, but the length of every life is ordained. Now that she is dead, there is nothing more we can do for her in life; we can only give her a funeral of the finest kind. That will allow us to show what devotion we still can, and may also bring some peace to the spirits of your late daughter and granddaughter.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia wept more bitterly than ever. Fearing that the old lady would be overcome by grief, and taking advantage of the fact that Baoyu was not fully conscious, Xifeng secretly sent someone to tell Grandmother Jia the comforting lie, “Baoyu is asking for you.” Only then did Grandmother Jia stop crying and ask, “Has something else happened?” Xifeng answered with a placating smile, “Nothing has happened. I expect he simply misses you.” Grandmother Jia hastily took Zhenzhu's arm, and Xifeng followed her over.

p.src: Halfway there, they happened to meet Lady Wang coming toward them, and she reported everything to Grandmother Jia in detail. Grandmother Jia was naturally stricken with grief once more, but as she was on her way to Baoyu, she had to hold back her tears and say sorrowfully, “If that is how matters stand, I shall not go there. You may arrange everything yourselves. It would only distress me to see it; just make certain that she is treated with all due care.” Lady Wang and Xifeng each promised to do as she said. Only then did Grandmother Jia go on to Baoyu. When she saw him, she asked, “Why did you send for me?” Baoyu smiled and said, “Last night I saw Cousin Lin come here. She said she was going back south. I don't think anyone else can persuade her to stay. Grandmother, you must keep her here for me.” Grandmother Jia listened and said, “Certainly. Set your mind at ease.” Xiren then helped Baoyu lie down.

p.src: Grandmother Jia came out and went over to Baochai’s quarters. At that time Baochai had not yet made the customary ninth-day return visit, so whenever she saw anyone, she showed a certain bashfulness. That day, seeing Grandmother Jia’s face streaked with tears, she offered her tea, and Grandmother Jia told her to sit down. Baochai sat beside her, her body turned slightly aside, and only then asked, “I heard that Cousin Lin was ill. Is she any better?” At these words Grandmother Jia’s tears streamed down unchecked. She said, “My child, I will tell you, but you must not tell Baoyu. It was all because of your Cousin Lin that you had to suffer so many grievances. Now that you are a married woman of this family, I can finally tell you. Your Cousin Lin has in fact been dead for two or three days; she died at the very hour you were married. Baoyu’s present illness is still on account of this. Since you all lived together in the Garden before, naturally you understand what lies behind it.” Baochai’s face instantly flushed crimson. At the thought of Daiyu’s death, she too could not keep from shedding tears. After speaking with her a while longer, Grandmother Jia left. From then on Baochai turned the matter over endlessly in her mind and devised a plan, but she would not act rashly; only after her ninth-day return visit did she settle upon this method. Now Baoyu was indeed somewhat better, and only then could everyone speak without being as guarded as before. Baoyu’s condition improved day by day, but his infatuated grief could never be dispelled: he insisted on going in person to weep for Daiyu. Grandmother Jia and the others knew that the root of his illness remained and forbade him to indulge in such thoughts; yet his pent-up anguish was unbearable, and his illness repeatedly relapsed. The physician, however, perceived that it was a sickness of the heart and advised that he be allowed to unburden his feelings; if medicine were then used to restore him, he might recover more quickly. Upon hearing this, Baoyu immediately asked to go to the Naiad’s House. Grandmother Jia and the others had no choice but to have a bamboo chair brought over and help Baoyu into it. Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang went on ahead. When they reached the Naiad’s House and Grandmother Jia saw Daiyu’s coffin, she wept until her tears ran dry and her breath failed. Xifeng and the others repeatedly consoled her until at last she stopped. Lady Wang also wept for a time. Li Wan then invited Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang to rest in the inner room, though she herself was still shedding tears.

p.src: As soon as Baoyu arrived, he remembered coming there before his illness; now the rooms remained while their mistress was gone, and he could not keep from wailing aloud. Remembering how close they had once been and that death had now parted them forever, how could his sorrow not deepen? Everyone had feared that excessive grief after his illness would harm him, and they all came to console him. But Baoyu was already sobbing as though he would die and return to life again, so they supported him to a place where he could rest. The others who had accompanied him, Baochai among them, all wept bitterly as well. Baoyu alone insisted that Zijuan be brought to him, so that he could learn exactly what her young mistress had said before she died. Zijuan had originally hated Baoyu deeply, but seeing him like this somewhat softened her heart. Moreover, with Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang both present, she did not dare vent her resentment on him. So she told him everything in detail: how Miss Lin’s illness had returned, how she had burned the handkerchief and consigned her poetry manuscripts to the flames, and what she had said before she died. Baoyu wept again until his breath caught and his throat went dry. Tanchun took the opportunity to repeat Daiyu’s dying request that her coffin be taken back south. Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang began weeping again. Fortunately, Xifeng’s eloquent words of comfort calmed them somewhat. She then urged Grandmother Jia and the others to return. Baoyu could not bear to leave, but Grandmother Jia compelled him, and he had no choice but to return reluctantly to his room.

p.src: Grandmother Jia was advanced in years. Ever since Baoyu had fallen ill, she had known no peace by day or night, and now, after this fresh bout of bitter grief, she felt dizzy and feverish. Though she remained anxious about Baoyu, she could no longer keep herself going and returned to her own room to lie down. Lady Wang’s heartache was still harder to bear, and she too returned to her quarters. She sent Caiyun to help Xiren care for Baoyu, saying, “If Baoyu grieves again, come and tell us at once.” Baochai knew that Baoyu could not let go of his grief at once, so she did not try to dissuade him, but merely addressed him with gently barbed remarks. Baoyu, fearing that Baochai might take his grief to heart, checked his feelings and wept silently. After a night’s rest, he passed the night quite peacefully. Early the next morning everyone came to see him. He was still weak and short of breath, but the sickness of his heart seemed to have eased somewhat. Thereafter they cared for him with redoubled attention, and he gradually recovered. Fortunately, Grandmother Jia did not fall ill, though Lady Wang had not yet recovered from the pain in her heart. That day Aunt Xue came to visit. Seeing that Baoyu was in somewhat better spirits, she too felt reassured and stayed on for the time being.

p.src: One day, Grandmother Jia specially invited Aunt Xue over to discuss matters with her. “Baoyu owes his life entirely to you, dear aunt. Now I think he is out of danger, but your daughter alone has had to suffer for it. Now that Baoyu has spent a hundred days recuperating and regained his former health, and your daughter’s mourning period has also ended, the time is just right for them to consummate their marriage. I should like you to take charge and choose another particularly auspicious day.” Aunt Xue replied, “Your plan is excellent, madam. Why is there any need to consult me? Though Baochai may seem rather simple and awkward, she understands things very clearly in her heart. You have long known what her disposition is like. I only hope that husband and wife will live together in harmony from now on. Then you will be spared a great deal of worry, my elder sister will find some comfort, and I too shall be at ease. You need only choose the day, madam. And need we notify the relatives?” Grandmother Jia said, “This is the first great event in the lives of Baoyu and your daughter. Besides, after all the twists and turns we have endured, they have only now found peace, so we must let everyone celebrate merrily for several days. All the relatives must be invited. For one thing, it will fulfill our vow of gratitude; for another, we can drink a cup of wedding wine. Then all the anxiety this old woman has suffered will not have been in vain.” Aunt Xue was naturally delighted to hear this and went on to speak at some length about preparing the bridal trousseau. Grandmother Jia said, “We are relatives joining our families still more closely, so I do not think all that is necessary. As for everyday furnishings, his rooms are already full of them. If there are a few things Baochai particularly cherishes and wants from you, dear aunt, you may bring those over. I do not think Baochai is one to brood over things. She is unlike that granddaughter of mine in temperament—and that is why the poor child was not destined for a long life.” As she spoke, even Aunt Xue began to shed tears. Just then Xifeng came in and said with a smile, “What have Grandmother and Aunt been thinking about now?” Aunt Xue replied, “The old lady and I were speaking of your Cousin Lin, and that made us sad.” Xifeng laughed. “Grandmother and Aunt, please do not grieve. I have just heard a funny story, and I thought I would tell it to you both.” Grandmother Jia wiped away her tears and said with a faint smile, “Who knows whom you are going to make fun of this time? Tell it, and let your aunt and me hear it. But if you fail to make us laugh, we shall not let you off.” Before Xifeng had even opened her mouth, she began gesturing with both hands and doubled over with laughter. What she was about to say will be revealed in the next chapter.
